### Observed differences

- The elapsed time between consecutive completions of A05 and A03 grew: in the earlier window the median gap was about 0.08 hours (roughly 5 minutes, mean about 0.11 hours), while in the later window the median was about 0.16 hours (roughly 10 minutes, mean about 0.19 hours) — an average increase of about 0.08 hours, i.e. roughly 5 minutes. [TWAIT001]
- The gaps also became more variable: the middle half of the gaps moved from roughly 0.04–0.15 hours to roughly 0.09–0.22 hours, and the standard deviation rose from about 0.09 to about 0.13 hours. [TWAIT001]
- These gaps were observed only rarely: 37 gap observations in the earlier window and 30 in the later window (about 19 and 15 per 100 traces respectively), so the comparison rests on few observations. [TWAIT001]
- The size of the time difference is unusual for random re-splits of the pooled data — it exceeds about 995 of 1000 reference comparisons — but a single such item is not, by itself, evidence of a structural change. [TWAIT001]

### Inference

Support level: Insufficient evidence

The evidence is insufficient to infer a structural change in the process. Only one item qualified, which is what an unchanged process typically produces given the screening expectation of about 0.32 items by chance across the 64 tested units; moreover, the item measures elapsed time between consecutive completions of A05 and A03 rather than structure, and it is based on only 37 versus 30 observations, so a timing shift (or sampling noise) cannot be ruled out. [TWAIT001]

1 item vs 0.32 expected — that's the same order (one item when fewer than one is expected). So the verdict must be "Insufficient evidence".

Also, T_WAIT is time-based, not structural. A time change alone doesn't directly support a structural hypothesis about order/placement. Even if we had more items, a wait-time increase between A05 and A03 doesn't directly show a structural change; it could be a timing change without structure change. But the primary gate is the screening comparison: 1 item ≈ 0.32 expected → insufficient.

Note: TWAIT is elapsed time between consecutive completion events; do not call it pure waiting/service/processing time.

Support counts: 37 and 30 — small samples, weak proportions.
